page: Vultr vcg-a16-48c-496g-128vram is a GPU-accelerated server instance within the Cloud GPU family. The hardware configuration features an Intel x86_64 processor with 48 shared vCPUs, derived from 24 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. System memory totals 496.0 GB, providing approximately 10.33 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance is equipped with eight NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined 128 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 1500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring 73907.77 in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and 55603.55 in the PassMark CPU test. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1781.09. Memory performance is robust, showing a strong read-only small block bandwidth of 4709.75 GB/sec and a strong large block write bandwidth of 101.16 GB/sec. The instance excels in LLM inference tasks, achieving top-tier prompt processing speeds of 8182.48 tokens/sec for a 135M model and 610.38 tokens/sec for a 7B model. Redis SET operations are also highly efficient, registering 74.78 million operations per second.

The shared CPU allocation model represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, dedicated single-core CPU performance. However, the high density of eight NVIDIA A16 GPUs paired with 496.0 GB of RAM offers a resource-dense profile for parallel processing tasks. This hardware composition makes the instance highly suitable for multi-stream video transcoding, remote graphics rendering, large-scale database operations, and medium-scale LLM inference workloads.
